endorsements.quote: CPD should strengthen skills in critical appraisal of AI outputs, bias awareness, explainability, and appropriate reliance on automated tools.
AI literacy and ethical oversight should become core organizational competencies.
Simulation is valuable for practicing responses to AI errors.

unlisted_practices: CPD programs should build capacity for human-AI teaming by supporting distributed cognition and coordinated human-AI decision making across clinical teams.
CPD programs and accrediting bodies should integrate guidance on ethical AI use, transparency, algorithmic bias, and responsible use in assessment and scholarly activities.
CPD should help clinicians address patient misinformation and guide patients' safe use of AI tools.
CPD providers should collaborate with institutional leaders to address tensions involving data governance, scope of practice, accreditation, and workflow redesign.
Faculty development should guide learners through AI-related identity and cognitive shifts.
Approach AI implementation in CPD as a redesign of the entire activity system, anticipating contradictions in roles, workflows, governance, and professional norms.
Periodically revise the framework as AI technologies and regulations evolve.

screen.reason: Theoretical framework paper integrating Cultural-Historical Activity Theory to examine AI's impact on continuing professional development and learning systems.
